requirements.requirement: The system must map backend malpractice measure data to one of three UI states: clean, flagged, or unknown.
The system must assign state 'clean' when backend indicates zero malpractice incidents within the defined evaluation window.
The system must assign state 'flagged' when backend indicates one or more malpractice incidents within the defined evaluation window.
The system must assign state 'unknown' when backend malpractice data is null, missing, or explicitly marked unavailable.
The system must not display the terms 'fraud', 'misconduct', or any legally accusatory language in malpractice-related UI text.
The system must generate neutral signal-based language describing malpractice status (e.g., 'no recent malpractice signals' or 'malpractice signals present').
The system must format score_contribution as a numeric value with consistent precision (e.g., one decimal place) suitable for display.
The system must calculate score_contribution based on the backend malpractice measure input without modifying backend-provided weights.
The system must default score_contribution to 0 when malpractice data is unknown or unavailable.
The system must ensure all generated malpractice display text is compatible with markdown-safe rendering in MessageBubble.tsx.
The system must ensure LLM-generated or templated text does not infer intent, blame, or legal judgment about the provider.
The system must ensure LLM-generated or templated text remains consistent for identical input data (deterministic output).
The system must handle exception case where backend returns malformed malpractice data by falling back to 'unknown' state without UI failure.
The system must handle exception case where score_contribution is missing or non-numeric by defaulting to 0 and logging the anomaly.
The system must ensure all malpractice-related display strings are derived from controlled templates or validated LLM outputs before rendering.
